extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners, communications students, and journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing public-relations and journalistic copy using Associated Press (AP) Style to maximize accuracy, consistency, readability, and alignment with newsroom expectations. Emphasizes core AP entries, inclusive storytelling, and fidelity to the AP Stylebook with allowable organizational customizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt AP Style as the standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Associated Press Stylebook as the foundation for journalistic and PR writing to achieve accuracy and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhering to a consistent style improves readability and brand recognition and establishes a common language with journalists; many PR employers expect AP-style competency and may test hires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the basics: Dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow AP rules for formatting dates in copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates are a recurring AP entry to memorize or consult in the stylebook; keep the stylebook handy for specific date formatting questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the basics: Numerals
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply AP numerals rules (when to spell out numbers vs. use digits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP generally spells out zero through nine but has many exceptions; consult the 'numerals' entry in the stylebook for contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the basics: Dollars & percents
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AP conventions for monetary amounts and percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the stylebook for preferred symbol use, spacing, and when to spell out amounts versus using figures and percent signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the basics: Times
rubrics_metrics.description: Format times according to AP conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the stylebook on use of a.m./p.m., noon/midnight, and how to present time ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the basics: Addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow AP formatting for street addresses, cities, states, and postal conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look up specifics (abbreviations, commas, ZIP usage) in the stylebook when unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the basics: Titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Format and capitalize job and honorific titles per AP guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP limits capitalization of titles; verify whether a title is used before a name (capitalized) or after/alone (lowercase) in the stylebook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the basics: Names
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AP rules for names, including how to introduce and subsequently refer to people and organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AP preferences for given names, last names, and honorifics; consult entries for complex or unfamiliar name formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the basics: Composition titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Format titles of books, films, articles, songs, and other works according to AP rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP has specific rules for quotation marks, capitalization, and when to abbreviate; check the stylebook for edge cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the basics: Abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply AP conventions for creating and using abbreviations and acronyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessary abbreviations; in most cases do not include an abbreviation in parentheses after a name; many abbreviations do not use periods; some acronyms (e.g., FBI) are acceptable on all references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the basics: Social media use
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow AP guidance for referencing and formatting social media content and identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the stylebook for conventions about handles, hashtags, links, screenshots, and how to cite or quote social-media posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: One preferred spelling per word
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the AP Stylebook’s preferred spellings; every word should have one and only one spelling in your copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the stylebook first for preferred spellings (e.g., adviser vs. advisor), then a dictionary if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize far fewer words than you might instinctively; limit capitalization to proper names and cases AP prescribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always look it up before capitalizing anything other than proper names; AP recommends conservative capitalization rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive abbreviation
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit use of abbreviations and acronyms; do not introduce needless parenthetical acronyms after names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including an abbreviation in parentheses immediately after a name usually is unnecessary; most abbreviations do not require capitals or periods per AP; however, some acronyms (FBI) are acceptable on all references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuate by generally accepted rules; omit Oxford comma
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard punctuation but follow AP’s exception for the serial (Oxford) comma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP style says not to use the Oxford comma in a series (example: 'The flag is red, white and blue'); otherwise punctuate according to generally accepted rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spell out zero through nine (with exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a general rule, spell out numbers zero through nine; many exceptions exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are numerous contingencies to this rule—consult the 'numerals' entry in the stylebook for specifics on when to use figures instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the AP Stylebook when in doubt
rubrics_metrics.description: When unsure about spelling, capitalization, numerals, abbreviations, or other style questions, look it up in the AP Stylebook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memorize a few core rules but keep a current copy (printed or online) on hand; the stylebook is updated annually and may contain significant changes some years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow organizational customizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations may adopt AP style as their base but customize specifics for their own naming, capitalization, or abbreviation conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common customizations include how to abbreviate an organization’s name or whether to capitalize internal boards/committees; document and enforce any house style variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive storytelling (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow AP guidance to ensure accuracy, fairness, and inclusion in storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AP Stylebook’s inclusive storytelling chapter calls for giving voice and visibility to underrepresented people, showing sensitivity about words/phrases, expanding sources and story ideas, including necessary context/background, striving to recognize and overcome unconscious biases, and using thoughtful and precise language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give voice and visibility to underrepresented people
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that people who have been missing or misrepresented in coverage are given opportunity to speak and be represented accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively expand sources and story ideas to include diverse perspectives rather than relying on the same usual sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show sensitivity about word choice and labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Use language that respects people and avoids stigmatizing or reductive labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer person-first or context-specific descriptions (example guidance: 'a person with a drug dependency' rather than 'an addict'; 'a 70-year-old marathon runner' rather than 'an elderly woman').

rubrics_metrics.name: Include necessary context and background
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide readers with context needed to understand people, events, and data accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context can correct misperceptions and prevent misleading or decontextualized portrayals; consult inclusive-storytelling entries for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and attempt to overcome unconscious bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of and actively mitigate unconscious biases in sourcing, word choice, and framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the stylebook’s guidance to identify common bias pitfalls and corrective practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use thoughtful, precise language
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose specific, accurate words rather than vague or loaded terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong writers prioritize accuracy beyond grammar; a single word can shape perceptions, so opt for precise descriptors and avoid stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow expanded pronoun guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect and use people’s pronouns, including singular they/them/their where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AP Stylebook expanded pronoun guidance; consult the entry for rules on usage, attribution, and how to handle nonbinary or gender-neutral pronoun choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference updated disability-related entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AP's revised disability-related guidance to refer to people with disabilities respectfully and accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2022–24 edition added 35 new or revised disabilities-related entries—consult them for person-first language, terminology, and accepted phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize accuracy in all choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Make accuracy the top priority in word selection, framing, and factual representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy includes grammatical correctness and choosing the words and structure that convey the most accurate version of a story; when in doubt about connotation or correctness, consult the stylebook and prefer specificity and context.
